Quota display studies

Every answer on this page is read from the answers file (ui-rules-answers.json, format answers/2): open or closed, who speaks, the limits, the gear and the licence. The rules export supplies only the words: labels, the book’s text and sources. Pick a water, a part and a date. Anything the answers file lacks is shown in a dashed red box, never worked out here.

Today’s card

One row per group of fish that share a limit. Open a species for its full rules.

E · for packing and buying

Gear & licence

What you need to hold and what you can put on your line, for this water today. Tap a tile for the detail.

G · for the people building it

Checks

The export’s sample waters and our own cases, each looked up in the answers file’s ladder and compared with the case. Open one to see every rule in play and why the rest are silent.

Every fish in a group counts toward the group. A rainbow trout with its own limit of 2 still counts toward the trout-and-char total, unless the book gives it its own larger number (then it is counted apart).
Zero has three spoken forms. Closed (you can’t fish for it), Release (fish, but let it go), and a size limit (“release any under 30 cm”). The number 0 never appears.
Open or closed comes first. The strip at the top shows the whole year with the chosen day marked. A closed water shows only when it reopens and a link to the rules from that day.
Sources are one tap away. Each line opens the rule it came from. “Sources” lists every rule behind a row, including the ones that were overruled and why.
